user_provided_notes: Inbound lead from our doc-search landing page — uses PaperKite name internally, building legal-document search for small law firms.
Primary goal: fast, accurate document search and answer generation for client docs with strong snippet-level recall.
Current stack: PostgreSQL for metadata, Supabase for file storage; experimenting with Weaviate and Supabase vector DBs.
Scale: ~120 employees, expected search QPS 5-20 depending on roll-out; burst to ~40 during peak.
Latency target: 200-500ms tail for retrieval+rerank+response in hosted setup. Cost sensitivity: high — need clear per-embedding + per-token estimates.
Use-case specifics: create embeddings of 1-2 paragraph chunks, store in vector DB, do initial kNN candidate fetch then pass candidates to reranker model for final scoring + answer generation.
Questions asked on call: How to format embeddings for Redwood hosted API? Can we stream partial results while reranking? Do you support batch embedding uploads?
Also asked: recommended embedding dimension / model, top_k for recall vs rerank tradeoff, support for MMR or diversity-based reranking workflows.

Security notes: SMB but legal data includes PII — asked about SSO/SAML for team access, audit logs, and where embeddings are stored (residency options).
They emphasized self-serve: 'we want to try hosted first, get ok latency and cost, then talk Dedicated only if residency/throughput forces it'.
Asked for a short POC plan: 30 days, ingest 3k docs, evaluate recall/precision with Redwood-hosted embeddings + reranker, cost under $1k/month for POC ideally.
SE recommended: use 512-token chunks, embed with open-embedding-small-v1 for initial pass (cost sensitive), then rerank with a 7B or smaller reranker — provided notes on tradeoffs.
Action items from SE: send sample SDK snippet (Python + JS) showing batch embeddings, upsert to Supabase, and candidate retrieval + rerank call to hosted API.
